thread:
maya: Quick q — who owns SLA-driven flag gating? We need flags to auto-pause rollout if p95 latency > 250ms sustained for 5m. Thinking: feature owner defines criteria + runbook, but ops owns circuit breaker and console signals. Thoughts?
raj: I'm leaning ops owning the circuit breaker. Feature teams should own the criteria and the post-mortem.
kevin: agree with raj. Also think we should codify the rule in the config schema. e.g.
```json
"pause_on_sla": {
  "threshold_ms": 250,
  "window_secs": 300,
  "action": "pause|notify",
  "owner": "team-slug"
}
```
emily: UX concern — console must show ownership label and current state, plus one-click re-enable gated by an audit checkbox. Also show recent triggers in a timeline.
maya: +1. How do we surface the telemetry? Can we reuse the SLO dashboard or do we need a lightweight signal endpoint? cc @ops
ops: We can emit a canonical event at /signals/flag-paused with metadata (flag, reason, at, p95). Need idempotent apply and a TTL to avoid indefinite pauses. For hosted customers we'll default to "notify" and require manual pause.
deploy-bot: Alert — trial flag rollout paused: flag=quick-embed, reason=p95>250ms, at=1699012400
raj: Important question: who signs off to re-enable? Ops or the feature owner? My preference: owner signs off after validation, ops can force-unpause in emergencies.
kevin: Implementation plan: add a "safemode" resource in config-api with fields {owner, auto_pause, sla_rule, failopen}. We'll need migration + policy for existing flags.
emily: UX mocks next week. Can we add a "why paused" toast linking to traces and the matching SLO chart? Also show estimated cost impact when paused.
maya: I'll draft an RFC with schema + API endpoints + rollout plan. Assigning: @kevin for API spike, @ops for runbook, @emily for UX. Timeline: propose canary rollout next Thursday.
ops: noted. Runbook note: add TTL + automatic re-eval flow so paused flags don't stay down forever if owner is OOO.
kevin: I'll spin up a quick spike today to prove the schema + event route. Please add edge cases (multi-flag rollouts, dependent flags) to the issue.
maya: thanks — issue: https://redwood-internal/boards/FLAG-1234
